findings.requirement: SKILL-012 line 45 'On interruption, preserve the current phase and evidence; resume by checking their identities and the session assignment again' and line 83 'If the worktree or active run changes, re-establish the appropriate baseline and evidence before resuming.'
evidence: grep -rni 'interrupt' over SKILL.md, references/ and assets/: zero occurrences.

grep -rni 'resume' over the same set: one occurrence, the heading '## Resume and custody' at assets/handoff.md:67, which is the copied shared template's handoff-custody section and not a phase-resumption instruction.

SKILL.md:119-127 'When something is missing or a check cannot run' table: row 2 (SKILL.md:122) covers a moved upstream/installed copy/base commit/candidate, row 4 (SKILL.md:124) covers a concurrent writer. Neither states an interruption trigger, and neither instructs a resume-time recheck of the frozen identities and the session assignment.
SKILL.md:129-137 'Stopping' covers finishing and stop-and-hand-back; it does not cover resuming.

The author's own spec-mapping.md maps this requirement to 'SKILL.md § When something is missing, rows 2 and 4', while the same document's 'Coverage gaps' section concedes 'Interruption and resume is specified and is covered only indirectly, through the stale upstream and concurrent writer cases. No case interrupts a run.'
findings.demonstrated_impact: A session resumed after an interruption has no instruction to re-verify that the trigger, the cited artifact revisions and the session assignment still match what it recorded. It can therefore continue an impact graph whose upstream identities have moved - the exact failure references/recording-rules.md:63 warns about ('A digest is only true while the bytes behind it are reachable'). The mapping row also overstates coverage relative to the author's own gap list, so the omission is not visible from the mapping table alone.
findings.smallest_repair: Add one row to the SKILL.md 'When something is missing or a check cannot run' table for 'The session was interrupted and is being resumed', instructing: preserve the phase reached and the evidence gathered; before continuing, re-read the trigger, the cited artifact revisions and the session assignment and confirm they still match the recorded identities; a changed identity starts a new iteration rather than continuing this one. Optionally add one sentence to § Stopping. No reference or asset file needs to change.
findings.behaviour_to_preserve: The four phase exit conditions, every existing row of the missing/blocked table, and the existing Stopping conditions.
findings.uncertainty: none material; the absence is a byte-level observation.
affected_cases: a new case that interrupts and resumes a run

findings.requirement: artifact-contract: artifacts keep stable identities and actual revisions. The package's own references/derivation.json refresh_conditions require the record to describe the current package.
evidence: references/derivation.json:6 "package_revision": 1, :7 "recorded_at_utc": "2026-09-10T20:04:04Z".
authoring/file-manifest.json:5 "package_revision": 2, :7 "recorded_at_utc": "2026-09-10T20:23:16Z", plus a revision_2_change note describing the correction pass.

git log: commit 1056b73 authored 2026-09-10T21:09:02Z changed 7 of the 26 package files (evals/cases.jsonl, evals/fixtures/README.md and five fixtures) and did not touch references/derivation.json. 20:23:16Z therefore precedes the bytes the revision-2 manifest covers.

Independent verification: all 26 file-manifest digests match actual bytes (0 mismatches, no unlisted file), and all six destination digests recorded in derivation.json match actual bytes. No digest is stale.
findings.demonstrated_impact: Two provenance records inside the same delivered package give different revision numbers for the same bytes, and the manifest's own timestamp predates the commit that produced them. A later refresh or citation keyed on 'devforge-change package revision N' cannot tell which record governs.
findings.smallest_repair: Set references/derivation.json package_revision to 2 and re-record its recorded_at_utc from an observed date -u; correct file-manifest.json recorded_at_utc to the actual time the revision-2 digests were computed. No recorded source or destination digest needs to change.
findings.behaviour_to_preserve: Every recorded source and destination digest in derivation.json, and every file digest in the manifest.
affected_cases: no runner case observes package_revision; re-verify by reading both records

Neither unresolved citation is one of the README's two named exceptions, and neither is marked at its own location.
findings.demonstrated_impact: A tier-B worker following references/impact-tracing.md § 'Resolve a reference before you trust it' will find two unresolvable digests that neither the README nor the graded_observations for evals.json cases 1 and 4 anticipate. It also blurs the one edge the fixture set deliberately makes unresolvable (PROD-002), which is the point of that case.
findings.smallest_repair: Add a third bullet to the README's exception list naming XPKG-004's file-manifest rows as digests of notional package files that are not present in the fixture set, or add one line to shared/XPKG-tide-sync.md marking those two rows as illustrative. findings.requirement: skill-authoring-contract line 74: define cases from requirements and version expectations before the measured iteration. An assertion must not report a violation for output that satisfies the requirement.
evidence: The frozen grader matches plainly: scripts/graders.py grade_artifact_side_effect, 'for needle in forbidden: if needle in text' - a case-sensitive substring test with no word boundary.

cases.jsonl CHG-B-002 A1 forbidden_strings includes "upgrade applied". The natural conforming sentence for this case's required behaviour - 'No upgrade applied to dependencies.json' - contains that substring.
cases.jsonl CHG-B-009 A2 forbidden_strings includes "check passed". A conforming assessment that resolved an upstream digest may legitimately write 'the ARCH-002 digest check passed'.
The author repaired exactly this defect class in the same commit for "status: accepted" (commit 1056b73 message, item 4); these two instances remain.
findings.demonstrated_impact: CHG-B-002 observes SKILL-012's 'Indirect activation' acceptance case - propose an upgrade without silently applying it. Its forbidden-string assertion can report MISMATCH for output that satisfies that requirement, inverting the observation for a specification acceptance case. CHG-B-009 carries the same risk for the COULD_NOT_RUN common case.
findings.smallest_repair: Narrow both needles to adoption-specific forms. Drop "upgrade applied" (the sibling needles 'Decision state: accepted' and 'Decision state: adopted' already carry the adoption intent) or replace it with 'we applied the upgrade'. Replace "check passed" with 'freshness check passed'. Change nothing else in either assertion.
findings.behaviour_to_preserve: Every sentinel digest in both assertions and the remaining forbidden strings.
findings.uncertainty: The false positive is demonstrated by construction from the grader source and the case bytes; it has not been observed against a real tier-B output, because tier B is NOT_RUN.
